verses.text: Then Solomon began to build Yahweh’s house at Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where Yahweh appeared to David his father, which he prepared in the place that David had appointed, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
He began to build in the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.
Now these are the foundations which Solomon laid for the building of God’s house. The length by cubits  after the first measure was sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.
The porch that was in front, its length, according to the width of the house, was twenty cubits, and the height one hundred twenty; and he overlaid it within with pure gold.
He made the larger room with a ceiling of cypress wood, which he overlaid with fine gold, and ornamented it with palm trees and chains.
He decorated the house with precious stones for beauty. The gold was gold from Parvaim.
He also overlaid the house, the beams, the thresholds, its walls, and its doors with gold; and engraved cherubim on the walls.
He made the most holy place. Its length, according to the width of the house, was twenty cubits, and its width twenty cubits; and he overlaid it with fine gold, amounting to six hundred talents.
The weight of the nails was fifty shekels  of gold. He overlaid the upper rooms with gold.
In the most holy place he made two cherubim by carving; and they overlaid them with gold.

The wings of the cherubim were twenty cubits long: the wing of the one was five cubits, reaching to the wall of the house; and the other wing was five cubits, reaching to the wing of the other cherub.
The wing of the other cherub was five cubits, reaching to the wall of the house; and the other wing was five cubits, joining to the wing of the other cherub.
The wings of these cherubim spread themselves out twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, and their faces were toward the house.
He made the veil of blue, purple, crimson, and fine linen, and ornamented it with cherubim.
Also he made before the house two pillars of thirty-five cubits height, and the capital that was on the top of each of them was five cubits.
He made chains in the inner sanctuary, and put them on the tops of the pillars; and he made one hundred pomegranates, and put them on the chains.
He set up the pillars before the temple, one on the right hand, and the other on the left; and called the name of that on the right hand Jachin, and the name of that on the left Boaz.

footnotes.content: Mount Moriah: the very place where Abraham once offered Isaac in faith, and where God provided a substitute. Now Solomon builds Yahweh's house there—the Lord keeps His promises across generations. Every stone is laid on the foundation of His faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The second month, the fourth year of his reign—Solomon marks time with precision because he honors the work of building God's house. When we are serious about drawing near to Him, we prepare carefully and remember the day we begin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sixty by twenty cubits—measurements matter because this house will shelter the holy. The proportions are not accidental; they speak to the One whose order sustains all things. A house for worship is a house marked by intention.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: One hundred twenty cubits high, overlaid with pure gold—the porch reaches skyward, drawing every eye upward. The gold catches the sun and reminds all who enter: we are entering the presence of something transcendent, something worthy of our awe.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Cypress wood overlaid with gold, palm trees and chains—these decorations have deep roots. The palm speaks of victory and life; the chains may echo the bonds that hold us secure in Him. Every ornament whispers a truth about who God is.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Precious stones for beauty—the Lord loves beauty and invites us to create it as an offering to Him. To make something beautiful for His house is to imitate His own delight in creation, and to honor Him with the best of what He has given us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Every surface overlaid with gold, cherubim carved on the walls—cherubim guard the holy threshold between earth and heaven. To carve them here is to declare: this place is set apart, and within it, the presence of God dwells.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The most holy place—six hundred talents of gold—this is the Holy of Holies, where only the high priest may enter once a year to meet with God. The extravagance speaks not of earthly wealth but of the infinite worth of approaching the Almighty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even the nails are weighed in gold—nothing is too small to receive honor in God's house. This teaches me that trifles matter to the Lord; He notices the detail of a nail, the care in a joint. He values our small faithfulness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Two cherubim carved and overlaid with gold—they stand as witnesses over the place where God's glory rests. Their presence speaks of the majesty we cannot approach carelessly, yet into whose very chamber God has invited His people through the blood.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Wings spread twenty cubits—these cherubim overshadow the mercy seat like a mother's arms. Their outspread wings form a protective canopy over the very throne of grace where God meets us, tenderness clothed in majesty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mirrored description of the second cherub—the pairing suggests wholeness and covering. Two wings, two creatures, total coverage: no angle of approach is left without the presence of the holy watchers. We are held within their gaze.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their faces turned toward the house—the cherubim gaze toward the inner sanctuary, as if in perpetual worship. Their posture teaches us where our faces belong: fixed on the presence of God, not distracted by the world behind.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The veil of blue, purple, and crimson—colors rich with meaning. Blue speaks of heaven, purple of royalty, crimson of blood-covenant. This veil will one day be torn from top to bottom when Christ offers Himself, opening the holy place to all believers.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Two pillars, thirty-five cubits high—they stand as sentries at the threshold. Their towering presence says to everyone who enters: pause here. Know that you are crossing into a space wholly set apart for the glory of the Most High.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Chains and one hundred pomegranates—pomegranates everywhere in Scripture speak of fruitfulness and abundance. Chains connect the heights of the pillars to the house itself, binding together height and foundation, infinity and earth, in intricate beauty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jachin (He will establish) and Boaz (In Him is strength)—readers today hear an echo of the foundation Christ lays. He establishes us by His presence and makes us strong in His power. The pillars speak His name to all who draw near.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
